title: With qualities, without
hookLine: the One is both beyond all qualities and present in every quality

cards: Is God far off, or right here? Put that to a room of people and the answers tend to split. Lean too far one way, and God is a distance with no one in it.

Lean too far the other, and God shrinks to a figure you could fit in a picture frame. Sikh scripture doesn't make anyone pick. It holds both answers in one breath, with two words that sound almost like twins.
Today's word is the first of them.

teach.b: Nirgun first. In the Granth's language, gun means a quality, a trait, the kind of thing you'd list to describe someone.
Nirgun is the One without qualities: beyond every description, past anything we could name, measure or picture. No shape, no color, no edge where it stops.
Then its twin, sargun: the One with qualities, present in every form there is, in the river and the mountain, in the stranger at the bus stop, in the patience of an old woman cooking for the langar.

In Sukhmani Sahib, Guru Arjan's long hymn of peace, one line holds both. In paraphrase: the One is without qualities, and the One is with qualities too. Not two gods, a far one and a near one taking turns.

One, both ways at once. Sikh teachers sometimes use the picture of the ocean and its waves: the ocean has no single shape, and every wave is still the ocean. Why does it matter on an ordinary afternoon?
If the One were only beyond, you'd have to leave the world to find it. If the One were only here, it would shrink to whatever you happened to like.
Together, nirgun and sargun keep both doors open: awe at what no one can hold, and tenderness toward what is right in front of you.

how: Sikhs speak of the One as nirgun, beyond all qualities, and sargun, present in every form, and Sukhmani Sahib, which holds both together, is recited by Sikhs at home and in gurdwaras.

o: a person who has given up all good qualities
the One beyond every quality or description
a hymn sung without any musical notes

games.q: with qualities, without: tap the pairs.

s: nirgun and sargun are two different gods
the same One, both ways at once.
Sukhmani Sahib says the One is without qualities and with them too
Guru Arjan holds both in a single line.
in Sikh thought, the One is only far away
sargun: the One is present in every form.

games.q: a friend asks you: is God far beyond the world, or right here in it? you have to answer.
o: beyond it, so look away from the world.
right here, so there's nothing beyond.
both: beyond every quality, present in every form.
games.why: Sukhmani Sahib doesn't make you choose: the One is nirgun and sargun at once.

practice: First think of the biggest thing you can, a mountain range, a desert, everyone who has ever lived, and let it be too big to hold.
Then bring your attention to something small and near: your own hand, a sound in the room, the next breath. If you pray, hold both as one; if not, just notice the shift from vast to close, and back.

wordCard.voice: Nirgun. The One without qualities, beyond every description, held together with sargun, the One present in every form. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: without qualities; its twin is ਸਰਗੁਣ, sargun, with qualities.

carryVoice: Your line: vast and close. Beyond every word, and in everything words touch. Rest well.
